is thankfully not my own medical practice, but I've been dealing with them for a while regarding my elderly parents.
This has to be the worst practice to telephone as at times, I've tried over 100 times once after the other to get through & all I've ever succeeded in doing is become irate & frustrated.
Last Wednesday, I tried to call for a routine appointment for my mum that her community nurse had advised I made & after numerous attempts, I finally got through.  The receptionist (who was rarher cold & unfriendly) told me that I have to call in first thing in the morning as that's when they deal with appointments. OK. Strange, but fair enough.
I tried first thing the next day & after 72 attempts (thankfully, I have the screenshot to prove it) I had the call answered only for to be in another queue. The usual you're number X in the queue, please wait to be connected. I think my hair grew an inch waiting.  A receptionist then came on the line & when I asked about making a ROUTINE appointment, I was advised that, oh no! They only do telephone appointments with a doctor & that I need an appointment for that. What???  I queried why I needed a telephone appointment when it was just a routine appointment whenever there may be a space. Well what do I need an appointment for? I'm asked. So I explain the reason why I need the appointment.   After all this back & forth, the receptionist did say that there was an appointment the next day (Friday) with Doctor Currans but that the doctor will call between 8.30 am & 6 pm.  That's fine, I said.  Even though i find this to be strange.  I stayed around the house the whole of Friday for the doctor ringing as I didn't want to be in Sainsbury's etc & have to discuss medical problems.  Nobody called me. I'm really annoyed after wasting a whole day on the lead up to the New Year when I could've been busy doing other things.  Today (Wednesday) was the first day back for staff, so I foolishly thought that someone might call today. Nobody called.
If a receptionist had even contacted me on the Friday & advised me that the doctor has been dealing with an emergency etc, I'd have been fine with that, but to be ignored completely, especially as I'd wasted so much time trying to book the appointment & been put through the mill trying to do so.  If there had been an appointment that my parents had missed, I can guarantee that there'd be a letter etc in the post advising that wasted appointments are a bad thing.  Why should it be fine when it's the surgery not keeping the appointment that they'd made me jump through hoops to  book?
It would be easier going up against Goliath than trying to get an appointment at this surgery., even if it is only a ROUTINE appointment that's requested.
There is the occasional receptionists that are great to speak to, but unfortunately, there are far too many that think they're better than me & know more than me & think they can diagnose the problem better than their practice doctors.  I, myself, as a nurse wouldn't presume to diagnose anyone over the phone.
I will certainly not be calling them again as they really should keep their appointments, but if need be, then I'll come in person & deal with it or take the issue outwith the surgery to the Scottish medical board.
It's a shame that this experience has been dire, annoying & frustrating as the doctors all appear to be really nice people, who are good at their jobs.  Something is severely lacking at this practice & i think the practice manager needs to take a look at their appointment booking procedures as they have to find better ways of doing this, or maybe they need a new manager with better ideas. I have never come across these issues in either my professional or personal life. I can only compare this surgery to my own, which is not far from them in distance, but is miles away in competence & manners.
